- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect potential rebound.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent spikes — if price spiked recently, forecast should be capped or smoothed to avoid lagged overcorrection.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3-5 consecutive days show downward trend, model often fails to anticipate reversal; add slight upward bias to forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to be overly optimistic in early forecast days (especially if sentiment is bullish); dampen initial forecast values.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model often misaligns with sentiment direction — align forecast slope with sentiment trend direction.
- When sentiment is flat (0.00–0.33), model often drifts toward historical mean — use sentiment as signal to adjust mean reversion strength.
